원자료 R01118의 적용 맥락: Analyzes U.S. household-level data (Consumer Expenditure Survey and CPS) for adults aged roughly 25–64 over the 1972–1998 period to document trends in cross-sectional income and consumption distributions. The paper studies how rising after-tax labor income inequality (and increases in idiosyncratic income volatility) coexisted with relatively stable consumption inequality, and interprets this in the U.S. institutional setting of evolving unsecured consumer credit markets and imperfectly enforceable contracts. It combines descriptive decompositions (between/within education-sex groups) with calibrated structural models to explain mechanisms.
